text:
Alex: Quick check-in — proposing a pragmatic path for SDK transport convergence. idea: thin per-language transport adapters + a small 'bridge' for browser cases. thoughts?
Maya: +1 to thin adapters. browsers are the messy bit. curious about gRPC-web vs websocket fallback.
Sam: Agree on adapters. Question: do we standardize on HTTP/2 streaming for native SDKs and only gRPC-web/websocket for browser?
Lina: That sounds reasonable. Node + Deno can do http2 and gRPC. Browser needs websocket or gRPC-web; ops prefers less protocol work in prod.
Alex: Precisely. Tradeoffs:
- HTTP/2 streaming: low latency, multiplexing, good for long lived KV-cache/decoder state. but proxies can break it.
- gRPC: typed, but heavier bindings per-language. gRPC-web solves browser but adds envoy/proxy layer.
- websocket: simplest in browser, but we lose HTTP semantics (headers) unless we surface them in frames.
Maya: For retries & pagination we need consistent semantics across languages. Should the transport surface resume tokens and per-request idempotency hints?
Sam: Yes. Proposal: all responses that can be resumed include a Resume-Token header/frame. SDK surface: iterators yield objects and expose "resume_token" on page boundaries.
Lina: Implementation nit: for streaming responses (chat/streaming tokens) we still need a way to snapshot a cursor. Maybe periodic checkpoints: every N tokens server emits a checkpoint frame with resume token.
Alex: Exactly. Checkpoints + explicit final resume token on chunk boundary. Client can opt-in to only checkpoint on safe boundaries to reduce noise.
Maya: Retries: client-side should retry idempotent operations only. For pagination/iterator, SDK should retry page fetches using the resume token, not naive rewind. Backoff: standard jittered exponential.
Sam: One more: deadline vs timeout. We should prefer per-call deadlines (propagated to transport) and a global SDK-level cancel.
Lina: Ergonomics: TS/Python expose async iterators. Go exposes an io-like Stream or channel. All adapters should implement a small interface: Connect(req) -> Stream with Send/Recv + Close.
Alex: Example adapter shape (pseudo):
```
interface TransportAdapter {
  connect(reqHeaders): Stream
}
interface Stream {
  send(payload)
  recv(): Message | EOF
  close()
}
```
Maya: Nice. That keeps SDK core transport-agnostic. We can implement http2 adapter, grpc adapter, websocket adapter.
Sam: For retries config: expose RetryPolicy { max_attempts, initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, retriable_codes }. Default sane values, but advanced users can tune.
Lina: Ops: the bridge (for browser) should be stateless and only proxy frames, with connection affinity to not break stream state. Could run as lightweight sidecar or edge lambda.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: new helm chart template created for bridge-proxy v1 (canary) — /deploy bridge-proxy/canary if you want to test.
Alex: Rollout plan:
1) land TransportAdapter interface in all SDKs (Python/TS/Go).
2) implement http2 + websocket adapters.
3) add resume-token checkpoint frames server-side and wire into adapters.
4) docs + samples for async iterators + retry policy.
5) optional gRPC adapter later if customers demand typed proto streaming.

Maya: Do we also add telemetry hooks in adapter (latency, connection-retries, frames-acked)?
Alex: yes — adapters should emit simple metrics: conn_open, conn_close, reconnects, frame_latency, resume_retries. keep names consistent across langs.
Sam: Concern: proxy behavior in corp networks. We should verify behavior through common corp proxies (Cloudflare, corporate proxies) in staging.
Lina: I'll add a runbook for bridge-proxy troubleshooting (sticky sessions, TLS passthrough).
Alex: Cool. Next action items:
- @Maya to draft SDK interface PR for TS + Python (this week).
- @Sam to spike a Go adapter using net/http2 (POC).
- @Lina to spec resume-token frame and checkpoint semantics for server.
- @Alex to coordinate bridge-proxy canary deploy per devops-bot notes.
Maya: I'll include example code for iterator resume:
```python
async for page in client.responses.paginate(req, retry_policy=default):
    process(page.items)
    if page.resume_token: save_token(page.resume_token)
```
Sam: LGTM. Keeping the transport layer small makes long-term refactors easier.
Alex: Thanks all — follow-up PRs when ready. :thumbsup:
